sections.heading: AI maturity: classical ML → ontology & relationships
bullets: Classical ML did not die — tree ensembles and anomaly scores still win many needle-in-haystack jobs. What’s changing is ambition: from feature-table scoring to entities, relationships, and governed meaning GenAI can be held accountable to.

Two pains that still burn budget: old AI — score dashboards when investigators need join paths across silos; new AI — copilots / naive RAG without shared vocabulary → hallucinations, wrong grain, PoC purgatory.
Mid-market reality: steep enterprise ontology platforms vs shallow auto-GraphRAG. The edge is relationship literacy and ontology-lite practices — not another horizontal “AI platform.”
Move now: keep classical ML where scores beat explanations; invest meaning/relationships where multi-hop GenAI fails — not “replace all ML with graphs.”

sections.heading: Databricks ontology-future pattern — what the market is building
bullets: Where the market is pointing: put governed meaning at the data layer, then use a living context graph so AI coworkers inherit governance — semantics upstream, agents downstream.

The pattern in one line: human-modeled metrics/definitions → inferred context with authority and permissions → coworkers/agents on that unified context (Databricks names this Metric Views / Genie Ontology / Genie One).
Why dual-stack still wins: that pattern grounds agents; it does not replace classical ML scores.
You don’t need a Lakehouse to start — Fabric, Bedrock GraphRAG, and Palantir are parallel futures; mid-market teams still win by learning the pattern first.

sections.heading: NetBird vs Defguard vs Headscale (WireGuard control planes)
bullets: NetBird: own clients + control plane; P2P WireGuard with Signal/Relay fallback; mesh + routing peers/exit nodes; first-class Authentik OIDC; Coolify ships netbird-client one-click (not the server).
Headscale: self-hosted Tailscale-compatible control server + official Tailscale clients; Authentik/OIDC supported; documented limit — OIDC groups cannot drive ACLs; lean ops.
Defguard: hub-and-spoke gateway VPN + IAM; native connect-time WireGuard MFA; external OIDC/Authentik is Business-tier — not any-to-any mesh.
Snapshot: NetBird wins mesh + IdP fit; Headscale wins Tailscale-client familiarity + sovereignty with ACL caveats; Defguard wins gateway + connect-time MFA when hub-spoke is the model.
Recommendation for Authentik + Coolify: 1) NetBird 2) Headscale 3) Defguard only if connect-time MFA / gateway model outweighs mesh.
